title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for operator-intent→device-configuration workflows in NetOps: translating natural intent into platform-specific CLI sequences, generating multi-step change plans, and proposing automated repairs. In production these proposals are typically not executed directly; deterministic validators, sandbox replay, staged canarying, and rollback mechanisms are recommended to convert model proposals into safe operational changes. The generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pattern—produce a candidate, check it with a deterministic analyzer, and apply automated or human-in-the-loop repairs—embodies this approach.

Despite conceptual consensus that validators and guardrails are necessary, practitioners lack controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier when the model’s proposal is held fixed. Without such measurements it is difficult to assess whether modest verifier investments (a deterministic validator plus a limited automated repair budget) materially reduce verifier-scoped safety violations when the LLM already produces high-quality candidates. To address this gap we executed a preregistered paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under canonical deterministic semantics. Our objective is narrow and operational: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone? The experimental evidence and all analysis artifacts are archived to permit deterministic re-inspection of every reported numeric claim.
sections.related_work:
Two literatures underpin this study. First, formal and deterministic network-configuration verification tools (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers and similar systems) have a long history of detecting reachability, isolation, and update-safety violations before deployment; such tools are widely recommended in NetOps practice because they provide concrete, mechanistic checks that are reproducible and explainable. Second, recent NetOps/AIOps research and system reports document the emergence of LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation and consistently argue for operational guardrails around model outputs. Generate–validate–repair or generate–critic architectures are commonly proposed across structured generation domains to reduce unsafe outputs; separate work catalogues systemic LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends deterministic validators or human oversight as mitigations.

What is less common in the published record is a controlled, preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms. Prior system papers typically evaluate end-to-end pipelines where generation and verification interact (e.g., verifier-guided regeneration), which conflates verifier detection with generation adaptation. Our study complements that literature by answering a distinct operational question relevant when deployment semantics require preserving the original proposal for human review or when model-call budgets constrain regeneration: how much verifier+limited-repair reduces verifier-scoped failures when the LLM proposal is fixed at the outset. This design isolates verifier remediation efficacy under realistic constraints (single repair iteration) and limited verifier coverage, making the measurement interpretable to operators choosing between deployment semantics and guardrail investments.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered (study_id = cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026). We froze inclusion rules, seeds, estimands, the confirmatory test, and the analysis executor before observing outcomes. The confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where per-task success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations over the verifier-modeled property set.

Task corpus and stratification. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was constructed with fixed generator seeds and stratified across three canonical clusters: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), and static-route-change (166). Tasks were constrained to the verifier’s modeled feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}) so the pass/fail outcome is defined relative to that coverage; tasks referencing unmodeled features were excluded by the preregistration rules and routed off-primary analysis.

Generation semantics and experiment control. To isolate verifier marginal effect we used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task we produced a single shared LLM proposal which served simultaneously as the baseline proposal and as the guarded arm’s input. The guarded arm ran a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) against that shared proposal and invoked at most one automated repair iteration only if the verifier flagged a preregistered high- or medium-severity violation. This prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates the effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the identical initial candidate.

Modeling, verifier and operational parameters. The requested model was gpt-5-mini (hosted adapter); generation used single-attempt calls with a 2000-token output limit. The deterministic validator maps concrete violation codes to severity levels and implements the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. The guarded arm permitted at most one repair call per preregistered contract. Execution accounting recorded model_calls_used = 501, where 500 were shared-initial generations and 1 was a repair-stage call.

Pre-specified inferential procedures. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) with the two-sided p computed by doubling the smaller tail probability and truncating at 1.0. We report the absolute paired-success-rate difference and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (B = 10,000; seed = 1729) preserving pairing during resampling. Missingness rules, retry policies, exclusion criteria, and multiplicity plans were fixed in the preregistration.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes. The run processed 500 complete paired tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with no confirmatory exclusions. Aggregated per-condition counts from the registered analysis executor are: baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency was n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, yielding an absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0020000000000000018.

Inferential outcomes and uncertainty. Under the preregistered exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention the two-sided McNemar p-value for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1) is p = 1.00. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). These results reflect the preregistered definitions and the small number of discordant pairs observed in execution.

Repair activity and corrected episode provenance. The guarded arm invoked a single repair-stage call; that repair produced the only discordant outcome (the one task where baseline failed and guarded passed). Execution accounting confirms exactly one repair-stage invocation (model_calls_used = 501; observed repair-stage calls = 1). The per-task validator diagnostics and repair traces recorded the violation code and the repair content for that episode in the archived evidence bundle; the deterministic reconciliation artifact confirms all accounting fields and stage counts.

Power, ceiling effect, and secondary analyses. The preregistered power calculation had assumed baseline failure prevalence ≈ 30% to detect a 10-percentage-point absolute reduction with 80% power. The observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) was far lower than anticipated, producing a ceiling effect: the study therefore had low sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements on the composite pass/fail metric. As a result, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts. All per-task outcomes and scoring traces are archived and were used as the exclusive basis for these aggregate statements.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation and scope. The measurement is conditional on multiple execution choices that operator teams should explicitly map to deployment decisions: single requested model (gpt-5-mini requested), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited property set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and allowance of at most one automated repair iteration. Within this constrained regime the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals on the verifier-scoped properties and the marginal pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). Importantly, a small aggregate effect size here does not imply the verifier lacks operational value: it corrected a concrete baseline failure and provides mechanistic diagnostics that would be necessary for human review and rollback planning in production.

Design trade-offs for deployments. The shared_initial_candidate semantics deliberately match operational scenarios where preserving the original proposal for audit or human review is required, or where model-call budgets make regeneration expensive. Alternative deployment choices—verifier-guided regeneration, larger iterative repair budgets, or multi-round synthesis—can increase the final-pass probability at the cost of additional model calls and increased complexity of audit trails; those semantics represent distinct operational interventions and should be measured under their own preregistrations.

Practical guidance derived from the evidence. First, measure baseline proposal error prevalence for verifier-scoped properties on representative operational data before allocating repair budgets: extremely low baseline error rates limit marginal return on modest verifier+repair investments. Second, align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints and expand the modeled property set if operators care about properties outside {admin, mtu, vlan} (vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, protocol state). Third, choose generation semantics to match priorities: shared_initial_candidate minimizes model-call overhead and preserves the original proposal for human oversight, whereas verifier-guided regeneration trades additional model calls for potentially larger final-pass gains.

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated execution accounting. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled property set: our success metric (no high/medium-severity violations) is defined relative to that coverage. External validity is constrained by single-model testing, a synthetic deterministic task corpus, and the specific validator implementation; results do not imply cross-model or cross-vendor generality. Statistically, the observed exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 follows the preregistered exact-binomial convention and reflects the small number of discordant pairs rather than evidence of equivalence; the paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.006] gives complementary uncertainty bounds for the absolute paired difference.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) isolating verifier+single-repair impact under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the preregistered exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is already very high relative to the verifier’s coverage, modest verifier+repair budgets yield limited measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric, yet can still remedy rare concrete failures. Practitioners should estimate baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, align verifier coverage with operational priorities, and select generation/repair semantics that match deployment constraints. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of these claims.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task corpus limited to the verifier-modeled features; task payloads were constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, wider cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or dynamic protocol states outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — we do not claim multi-model or cross-validator generality.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) induced a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the preregistered exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in the study evidence bundle. The run-level manifest and per-task scoring traces confirm exactly one such corrected episode in the confirmatory set.
